What I am building toward: the ground under you lights up for reach, the walk pad you already hold carries the enemy's beat, the bar says whose turn it is, the phone tells you afterwards what it cost, and ONE new thing for the weapon you are holding. Thirty things become five, and four of them already exist.

items.title: THE GRID: A CELL IS 32 PIXELS, YOU ARE ONE CELL, A HOUSE IS ABOUT 4 BY 4
items.why: You said the character stays tiny and moves one grid at a time, and one house does not equal one tile. Default sizes so everyone builds the same grid: a cell is about 32 pixels on your phone (about 11 across the screen), you fit in one cell, a house is about 4 by 4 cells with a door and an inside, a car is 2 by 1, a street is 3 cells wide with a 1-cell sidewalk each side. Every cell is one of five things: floor, wall, door, cover, prop. Up keeps these. Down and say which number is wrong.

items.title: THE ONLY HIGH GROUND IN THE FIGHT
items.why: You made one call about ground in a fight: ONE terrain rule, high ground helps you aim, and nothing else on a tile changes a number. I went and checked what the game already builds for that, and this is it, photographed in a real fight I walked into off the street. Then I counted it over 120 fights. A tile is one house, 12 metres. The raised slab turns up in 71% of fights. IT IS NINE HOUSES ACROSS, about 111 metres, so it is a city block with a staircase, not a mound. The nearest way up is 6 houses away. You start on the ground 120 times out of 120. So the one rule you kept changed 0 of 519 shots. It has never once fired in a fight anybody has played. The good news is there is nothing to delete: the game never grew Battle Brothers' hills and swamps and forests, so high ground really is the only ground rule in here. What I want to do next is make it a MOUND: something small, one house, that you are standing on or one step away from, so taking the height is a move you make in the fight instead of a building across the street. And when you are up on it you should SEE it, not read a plus sign. Thumbs up and I build the mound that way. Thumbs down and tell me if you would rather keep the big raised block and just make it reachable.

items.title: HOW YOU CROSS THE MAP
items.why: You said the valley gets crossed the Battle Brothers way, a marker you send somewhere while the clock runs. FIRST, WHAT THE MAP DOES NOW: I pressed the walk pad twenty-four times in all eight directions while zoomed out and he moved ZERO. The same press on the street moves him twenty-two lots and shifts three quarters of the screen. There is no marker and the pad is dead out there. So how should it travel? Battle Brothers slides its marker smoothly in real time and lets you pause. Your own rule says everything moves on the beat, twice a second, street and city both, one game mode. Those cannot both be true. A is their way, B is on the beat, and I picked B and built it because it is your own two rules agreeing and it is the walk feel you already voted for. They cover the SAME ground: B just stops at every beat and moves twice as fast in between. Say A and I switch it.
items.said: the valley is crossed on a MAP the Battle Brothers way: a party marker, tap where to go, time passes

items.title: THE ONLY PUMP
items.why: The Battle Brothers revamp says a place is a block and its buildings are what it offers. I built that and then counted the valley: 467 blocks, 215 of them offer nothing at all, and the ones that do are 249 shops, 12 sheds, 7 fortresses and ONE PUMP. The whole valley drinks through a single block. Battle Brothers towns have three to eight things attached to them; ours have one or none. So this is that block, from the camera you play on: two pumps, the pipes, the fence, the gate shut. The wrong thing is the path. There is only one worn into the yard and it goes to the electrical cabinet, not to the pumps. Somebody comes here a lot and only ever touches the switch.

items.title: WHO IS THAT ON THE ROAD
items.why: Parties roam the map now, so I drew all thirteen factions moving on it. TAP THIS, IT PLAYS. But first the thing I found. Your thirteen faction colours are yours, measured off your own clothes, and they stay. I measured what they do as banners on a map. CARTEL AND MOB ARE THE SAME COLOUR. They are 3.6 apart on a scale that goes to 373. Eight more pairs are under 50. And nine of the thirteen are the same brightness as the city ground they would be standing on. Eight of them are brown and four are grey, because this is a valley of working people in dust, which is right. It just means you can never tell who is coming by the colour of the flag. So the SHAPE tells you what they are and the banner tells you who. Four shapes: someone on foot with a flag, a patrol in a rank with points over it, a caravan with a canvas and wheels, and a crowd carrying their bedding. Which faction gets which shape comes from each faction's own canon alignment in the game files, not from me. Thumbs down and tell me which two you still cannot tell apart.

items.title: THE SAME STREET, THREE TIMES
items.why: One block. Three dates. Top is the ruin, which is the picture you already gave a thumb up. Middle is the same street reclaimed: the road patched, the power back, solar on a roof and a battery cabinet beside it, the line restrung. Bottom is the same street paying for itself: a second array across the road, the kerbs and the walks rebuilt, a second lamp, and the dead lot turned into a battery swap stand you can work at night. Nothing is ever taken away between one picture and the next, because you said the ruin is the floor. The machine counts that, it does not just say it. And one thing never changes in any of the three: the third house has its lights on and nobody lives in it, in all three acts. Everything around it gets better twice over and it never does. Thumbs up and this is how the city screen draws the act you are in. Thumbs down and tell me which act is wrong.

items.title: THE THIRTEEN ARE WEARING IT NOW
items.why: You said fire on the thirteen new runway shapes, so the thirteen groups put them on. This page PLAYS: every body walks at the speed the game runs at, standing on the street's own road and sidewalk, at the size the game draws a person. Four of them are here instead of thirteen, because these four are the ones that nearly lost their colour when the new clothes went on. The new clothes were searched on SHAPE, so every one of them came out grey or bone, and dressing everybody in them would have washed the colour out of eleven of thirteen groups in one go. Seventeen new colourways fixed that: same coat, same cut, the group's own colour, one line each, no new art. Nobody lost their colour and nobody changed body. Thumbs up and this is who is on your street. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the cut, the colour, or the boots.

items.title: WHAT THIS VALLEY STRIKES ON THE HOUR
items.why: You said the overworld is Battle Brothers and that time passes while you travel. You also said their map is a bunch of still pictures and we put life into it. So the map gets a clock you can HEAR. None of these three has one noise generator in it, which is the thing you killed three sounds over: they are metal being struck, and the notes inside each one are the real ones. A bell founder tunes a bell to a MINOR THIRD, which is why every bell you have ever heard sounds sad, and that is A and B. A struck pipe is not a chord at all, its notes sit at odd spacings, and that is why it clangs instead of ringing: that is C. A is a cracked bell, which is the realistic one for a valley nobody has maintained in ten years, so it leads. B is the same bell uncracked: its low note rings a second and a half after the high ones have gone, which is why a real bell seems to warm up as it fades. C is no bell at all, just a length of steel pipe, because that is what a dead town actually has. Tell me what this valley strikes.
options: A, a cracked bell
C, a length of pipe
B, a bell that still works

items.title: THE DECK IS NOT THE HISS
items.why: You killed the tape and you said it all sounded like sand. You were right: it was a band of hiss with a machine's name on it. This is the same idea rebuilt out of the machine instead. A tape deck is plastic being knocked and wheels turning, and hiss is the one part of a cassette a phone speaker would never pick up anyway. Press play and you get the lever, the head arriving 45 ms later, and the song SLIDING UP to speed, which is what a real deck does and what a whoosh was standing in for. Nothing in it is a number I picked: the standard says the tape moves 4.7625 cm a second, so the capstan turns 7.58 times a second and the reel 0.69, and those two are the wobble you hear. And the best part is free: the wobble gets SLOWER as the side plays, because the tape piling onto the reel makes it fatter. Same machine, slower breath. That is why a tape sounds tired instead of broken. Zero noise generators in it.
options: A, the whole deck
B, just the machine, no song
C, a worn-out deck

items.title: A FLIP IS A TAPE CHANGING
items.why: You said the old flip was kinda dogshit. It was hiss too, and it also claimed to be a radio while being built wider than any radio. This one is what the law already said a flip is: a tape changing. The flip is ONE TAP and it is always there, so you will hear it hundreds of times, which means the way it fails is not too quiet, it is I am sick of it. So: inside one beat, no riser, no whoosh, no sting, just the shell seating and the machine taking it. It is honest about what it is not, too: a real tape change takes several seconds, so this is the part of one you actually hear. The knock is a polystyrene shell ringing its own notes, which come from its shape and not from a setting. Zero noise generators in it.
options: A, the shell seats and the machine takes it
B, one knock
C, the old one comes out first

items.title: THE ONE WHO FELL IN
items.why: Nobody has ever walked with you in this game. Now somebody tells you what they used to be, and if you do not walk off, they come with you. Every picture is the walked street from the game's own camera. Is this the companion you want, and is one at a time right?

items.title: TERRITORY SURVIVES THE REBUILD
items.why: You just asked if we have to restart the whole enchilada for the new honest grid rule. For this lane, no. Territory lives one size up: the valley is 9,216 lots and fourteen crews own them, and that layer is untouched by your new rule, which only rebuilds what is INSIDE one lot (floor, wall, door, a house four cells across). I checked the actual numbers instead of assuming, and none of them collide. Everything this lane has measured and built, who owns the valley, the memory that lets a lot change hands and stay changed, still works exactly as it is. Nothing to vote on breaking here, just the reassurance with the numbers behind it.

items.title: IT IS NOT THREE GENERATIONS. IT IS THREE CRISES ON ONE MAP.
items.why: Battle Brothers never has generations. A brother dies, you hire another, and the company keeps its name, its crowns, and what every noble house thinks of it. The only thing that changes the world is a CRISIS: a war, an invasion, a plague of undead, that redraws who holds what without ever redrawing the map itself. That is closer to what your three acts already are than 'three lives' is. Same streets in all three, always. What changes is who holds them and what still works, which is exactly a Battle Brothers crisis. Research only, nothing to look at yet.

show.src:
NO GENERATIONS. ONE COMPANY, ONE MAP, THREE CRISIS CHECKPOINTS.

Battle Brothers has no fold, no time skip, no heir screen. Men die constantly and nobody notices, because the company is a name and a ledger, not a body. What changes the world is a CRISIS: same roads, same rivers, same towns, but who holds them and what they need is rewritten.

Our three acts already work this way and did not know it. One seed. One layout, 4,459 bytes, never rewritten. Measured on the real map this round: 6,899 ground pixels compared across all three acts, zero moved. Only what is lit and who owns it differs.

So stop saying generation. Say crisis checkpoint. Act 1 is before the crisis is answered. Acts 2 and 3 are the same crisis, further along, because the company (you, standing in three bodies) did more about it.

items.title: ONE HOUSE IS NOT ONE TILE
items.why: You said it: one house does not equal one tile, it is all fucked up. So here is the fight board you have right now, on the left, photographed in a real fight I walked into off the street. A tile is a whole house, 12 metres, and your phone holds TWO of them. That is why a fight feels like standing in a car park. On the right is the same picture with the new grid drawn on it. A cell is 32 pixels, so the phone holds 12 across and 20 down. A house is 4 by 4 cells, which makes a cell 3 metres and keeps a house at 12 metres, so nothing about the world changes size, only what a step is. Your man goes from 112 pixels to ONE CELL. Now the part worth looking at. The three squares are your reach, and I did not change a single distance you already picked: pistol 4 cells is still 12 metres, rifle 8 is still 24, scope 12 is still 36. Look what happens. Only the pistol fits on the phone. The rifle fills the whole board and the scope runs off the edge. That is not a bug, that is what a rifle actually is, and the fight camera already pulls back to hold everybody, so a rifle fight opens the shot by itself. Thumbs up and I build the fight on these cells. Thumbs down and tell me if your man is too small at one cell, or if a cell should be bigger than 32.

items.title: THIS ONE IS ALREADY DEAD, NOTHING TO TAP
items.why: This was your small character shrunk down small. You already killed the idea behind it in your last votes: you said not to make a whole new tiny character, keep the same one, same detail. So this does not need a thumb, it is already dead. I wrote down what happened and why in the records so nobody builds it again by mistake. Nothing for you to do here.

items.title: HE WALKS AT ONE CELL
items.why: You said the character is tiny again, one cell, one step per cell. First thing I had to answer: cut the big body down to one cell, is there still an animation in there? YES. All eight directions stay eight different pictures, nothing turned to mush, zero stray floating pixels. He is 24 rows tall with 168 lit pixels. The big art stays the source, like you said. BUT IT FOUND SOMETHING BROKEN THE WHOLE TIME, AT EVERY SIZE: the walk is built on a wave, and a wave is at zero twice per step, so frames 1 and 3 came out exactly the same picture on all six side-on directions. The side walk had THREE pictures, not four, and running too. At the big size you might not notice; at one cell it reads as a limp. A real walk's two middles differ because one leg is passing forward and THE PASSING FOOT CLEARS THE GROUND. That is the missing fourth picture and it is how legs work. This one PLAYS, with a panel at his actual size so it cannot flatter itself.
items.said: your character stays tiny even as you zoom out

items.title: STRUCK DOWN IN A FIGHT: 20% DEAD, ELSE OUT FOR 30 TO 40 DAYS WITH A MARK
items.why: Your words: only a 20% chance your character can die, otherwise a debilitating injury. Default: when one of yours is struck down, one in five dies for good and the company remembers. The other four in five live, are out of every fight for 30 to 40 game days, still cost their day, and keep a permanent mark: a scar, a limp, a lost eye, a stat that never comes back. Up keeps 20% and 30 to 40 days. Down and give me the number you want.

items.title: THE FIGHT IS ON CELLS NOW
items.why: You said one house does not equal one tile. It does not any more. Both of these are a real fight I walked into off the street on a phone, one build apart. On the left a tile was a whole house, 12 metres, 196 pixels, and the board held TWO of them. On the right a cell is 3 metres and 32 pixels, and the same phone holds 12 across and 20 down. Your man went from 112 pixels to one cell. Look at the right one: that is a street you could actually walk down, with a sidewalk and a road, instead of standing in a car park. Here is the part I care most about. NOT ONE DISTANCE YOU PICKED MOVED. A pistol was 1 tile and is now 4 cells, which is still 12 metres. Rifle 8 cells, still 24. Scope 12, still 36. Only the unit changed, and I did not touch the accuracy either. Two things I am not hiding from you. Your man is small now, and that is just what one cell costs. And the thumb ring in the corner is big next to the new board, which is a thing I already owe you a fix for. Thumbs up and I keep building the fight on these cells. Thumbs down and tell me which of those two is the problem: the man being small, or the ring being big.

items.title: THE WATER YOU COULD STAND ON
items.why: This is not a drawing, it is the dam pulled straight out of the game and coloured by one question: can you stand here. Green means you can walk on it. Grey is something solid. Top picture is what the game actually believed: THE WHOLE RESERVOIR IS RED, and red means you could walk out onto it. Over a third of that block was water you could stand on, 5,832 squares of it, plus the creek at the fort. It happened because every square has a word saying what it is, one list decides what each word does, and the word water was not on the list. Anything not on the list quietly becomes floor. Bottom picture is the same block after the fix: the water is water again and nothing else moved. Empty fountains and drained pools are still floor like they should be. Thumbs up and the blue is what deep water looks like from now on. Thumbs down and tell me what water should do to you instead.

items.title: WHAT THE BAR SAYS
items.why: B IS IN THE GAME NOW. You said build it and don't ask, so I did: on the map the top strip says your batteries, the hour and where you are, and the hour ticks while the party travels, the way Battle Brothers shows time passing. Before, it said nothing: one NOTES button on black, and the only clock was the tiny one on the phone. Every number is the game's own. A is what it was. C adds the day and who is with you, the Battle Brothers count of five. Tap A or C only if you want it changed.

items.title: RESHUFFLE ONE. TYPE ONE. PICK A SEX.
items.why: You said the three come prepared like Battle Brothers, with a reroll and a way to type your own. Here it is, shot on the real phone before and after. Left: the three prepared, Reyna, Ezekiel, Perla. Right: I tapped the little circle on the middle face to reroll just that one (Ezekiel became Araceli, the other two never moved), typed a name over the first one myself (Guadalupe), and picked a sex for the third (Jonah). One thing I am not hiding: the little faces did not change when the names did. That is a real gap and it is written up, not hidden behind a lucky screenshot. Thumbs up and this is how you set up your three when the naming screen ships. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the reroll, the crop, or the faces staying still.

items.title: THE VALLEY STILL BROADCASTS
items.why: Your own bible says the machines keep talking and never acknowledge you. Nothing in the game does that yet, and this is the one place a transmitter's band, hiss, wobble and drop-outs belong by right. I built it two rounds ago and then killed three sounds for sounding like sand in the same round, so I pulled this one out of your queue myself: its carrier was the same band-limited noise you had just rejected, and putting it in front of you anyway would have been the fourth sand sound in a row. Now it is rebuilt from real material. A transmitter's hiss is really two things: the power supply's own ripple (the same 60 Hz hum this valley's grid already has everywhere) and atmospheric static, which is not a smooth hiss at all, it is distant lightning arriving as separate clicks. Ten years of nobody buys more of both: a corroded antenna lets in more clicks, and a dried-out filter capacitor lets more ripple through. Zero noise generators in it. A plays it the way a maintained station sounds, B is the same signal off a machine nobody has touched in ten years, C is B on a loop, which is how you would actually meet it.
options: A, as it left the station
B, as it arrives ten years later
C, and it never stops

items.title: 48 QUESTS ALREADY CUT FOR OUR WORLD
items.why: You asked for volume and nothing built. This round read the whole library and cut 48 quest designs for Bohemia, filed by act, by crisis, and by boom or bust. It also wrote 8 rule pages the builders follow. Nothing is in the game. Thumb down if the rules below are wrong.

show.src:
THE RULES ALL EIGHT PAGES AGREE ON

1. The pay is said out loud before you say yes, and it never changes after.
2. Saying no writes nothing. Nobody frowns, nobody brings it up, ever.
3. Once you take a job, the only way out is in the world: tell the person to their face, or let their deadline pass. That is the only thing people remember.
4. Most jobs have no twist. About one in four does.
5. The place asks before the person does: an empty shelf, one dark window, a line at a dry pipe.
6. The first minute of the game nobody talks. You still have something to find within six steps.
7. Events on the road always have a cause you can see on the map, one per trip at most, and 'keep moving' is always free.
8. The family story lives on the one main quest. The jobs you took come back at the end as the people who show up for you.

48 designs: act 1 has 16, act 2 has 13, act 3 has 11, and 8 run across acts. 1,220 findings cited from 151 of the 152 quests you collected.

items.title: WHO YOU WERE THE DAY THE MONEY DIED
items.why: Your four origins. Three of them were already written into this game weeks ago and nobody noticed: the casino floor is the four trades that kept nothing when the city died, and that is why it is the hard one. I did not pick which is hardest, it is counted. Both pictures are the walked street from the game's own camera: the same man saying what he can still do, then saying it after he went down and could not. Is this the right four, and is the casino floor the one you would play?

items.title: SIX MORE WALKS HAD THE SAME LIMP
items.why: Last round the plain walk turned out to be drawing THREE pictures instead of four, because a step has two middles and the code drew them as the same picture. So I asked that of every other way this guy moves. NINE MORE WALKS, SIX OF THEM HAD IT, AND FOUR WERE BROKEN IN EVERY SINGLE DIRECTION: tired walking, swagger and walking with the gun out on all 8; sneaking 7 of 8; wandering 5 of 8; shoving something 4 of 8. Forty of forty-eight. Drunk, sprinting and scrambling were already fine because each carries a second wobble on a different clock, and that is the only reason they escaped. Fixed the same way, but THE FOOT CLEARS A DIFFERENT AMOUNT FOR EACH WALK, because they are different walks: a crouch and a shove keep the foot down, a stroll lifts it, a swagger is meant to be seen. It was in the shared facing-you code too, at the source. How much of his body changes between those two middles: it was ZERO for all six, and the machine check refuses zero now. AND I BROKE THE COAT DOING IT and the coat's own checker caught me: the first lift made the trenchcoat jump 26% of itself in one frame, so I swept four sizes and took the biggest one the coat does not notice at all. This one PLAYS, at full size (it first showed a tiny one-cell cut, which you killed, so that is gone; the fix never depended on the size).
items.said: your character stays tiny even as you zoom out

items.title: BATTLE BROTHERS SCHOOL: WHERE A BODY SPENDS ITS PICTURES
items.why: Battle Brothers has NO BODY on the map at all, just a marker with footstep sound, and in the fight it spends everything on the moment a weapon lands, not on the walking. I counted ours with the game's own counter: WE SPEND THE SAME ON A STROLL AS ON A PUNCH, and the most animated thing our guy owns is playing air guitar, at nearly twice the budget of a spear through the chest. The obvious answer is to move pictures from the walk to the hit, AND THAT IS WRONG FOR US: their fighter is a big sprite seen close, ours is now one cell, about 24 rows of body, and a hit that small cannot carry eight readable pictures. What a one-cell body CAN read is the silhouette changing, which is walking language. So my call: at one cell the walk keeps the pictures and the hit gets carried by sound and by the board. Up keeps that. Down and the hit gets the frames instead.

items.title: NOT STRANGERS ANYMORE
items.why: Your own phone strip has said since the flip shipped: the three faces are placeholders, not your family yet. That is fixed now, and it turned out worse than I thought before I measured it: ALL THREE were random rolls, not just the two older ones. The bridge that hands the strip a face only ever recognized the exact word you, so even Reyna at zero years was a stranger. Here are the same three slots, before and after, played on the real clock so you can watch them, not a still. Measured on things you can name about a face (haircut, hair colour, skin, eye colour, shades, hat, stubble, shirt, a braid), against 50 strangers who average 4.4 things apart from you: before the fix, Ezekiel and Perla were 3 and 4 things apart, no different from strangers. After, they are 1 and 2. And because the size you actually meet these three at is 26 pixels on the phone, not the 132 this card shows them at, the true-scale row is here too so the claim is honest about what you will actually see. draft:true: I picked both weights myself, you have not corrected either yet.

items.title: THE CELL IS THE STEP
items.why: Your 7/28 tiles, cut to the new cell, and one whole block built out of them. Top of the page: every cell next to the tile of yours it came from, so you can see nothing got redrawn behind your back. Five of them are your pixels and nothing else. Four are your material with one edge added, because your wall is drawn as a FACE and looking down at a street you need a CAP, and no picture of a cap exists at any size. Bottom of the page: one block whole, at your phone's own width. Now the thing worth looking at. HOW BIG IS A CELL? The law gives six numbers and they do not agree. One cell per step says 0.75 metres. Your own 7/28 tile bank says 0.75. Your own drawn car, which is already drawn from above, measures 0.80. But a car at 2 by 1 says 2.25 and a house at 4 by 4 says 2.90. Your own sentence and your own two drawings all say 0.75, and two round numbers say 3. I built 0.75 and here is why, in one line: at 3 metres a cell your whole approved tile bank is at the wrong size by four and every tile has to be drawn again, and at 0.75 it cuts straight across, which is what this whole page is. Look at the car sitting in the road next to the house. The car is as long as the whole house. That is the 4 by 4 being wrong, not the car. COMBAT shipped 3 metres this same round off the house number, so one of us is drawing at the wrong size and it is a number for you, not for us. Up keeps 0.75 and a house gets bigger, about 15 by 17 cells. Down and say 3 and I redraw the bank.

items.title: THE MAP DRAWS AT THE PHONE'S FULL PIXEL COUNT UNTIL BATTLE BROTHERS' NUMBER IS MEASURED
items.text: Your ruling: the map has as many pixels as the Battle Brothers map, exactly, as the bare minimum. Until DIRECTION measures that number off real screenshots, the floor is one painted pixel per screen pixel at your phone's own ratio (no scaled-up blocks anywhere on the map). DOWN means you want a different floor named.

items.title: THE STRIP IS THE ONLY SPECIAL PLACE YOU WALK, UNTIL YOU NAME ANOTHER
items.text: Tile-to-tile through the city is dead. You are on foot in the fight and in special places. The Strip is the one you named, so it is the only walked place for now. DOWN means you have more places in mind; say them in a note.

items.title: HOW YOU KNOW SHE IS WITH YOU
items.why: Somebody walks with you now. In the real game Estella Gaines lost her work, told you about it, and fell in beside you. But look at the screen: the only thing that says she is yours is her body, and your body is standing in front of it. Her name shows only while she talks, and the little gold name tag at her feet is under your boots. In Battle Brothers you can never forget who is in your company, because their faces never leave the screen. So, one question: A is what you have now. B puts her face in the top bar with a gold ring that empties when she gets hurt, in the spot the song title had. C puts nothing up top and marks her instead: a gold ring on the ground at her feet and a small mark over her head. It matters more after your last votes: places become settlement screens and you only walk in fights and special places, so most of the time her body is not on screen at all. And if she gets hurt and sits out for a month, only B still shows her.

items.title: 96 QUESTS ON THE SHELF, NOW ON YOUR CONTRACT SCREEN
items.why: Round two, built to your settlement contract screen the moment you said it. Nothing is in the game. Thumb down any rule below you hate.

show.src:
WHAT CHANGED THIS ROUND

1. Every job is a Battle Brothers contract now: you walk into a town, tap the hall, a face offers the job with the pay, you haggle, you take it or leave it.
2. The pay is worked out from days, danger and how scarce things are, never typed in by hand.
3. Push the haggle too far and the offer closes for that visit. Nothing else. Nobody holds it against you.
4. A crisis never runs a countdown. It changes what each town's board is offering.
5. No loyalty meter for your company. You see loyalty in how they fight, and some of them quit.
6. Every old quest we wrote was checked against the phone checklist. None passed. 14 become contracts, 11 become road events, 12 stay story beats, 5 are retired.

96 designs now: act 1 has 31, act 2 has 34, act 3 has 22, and 9 run across acts. All 152 quests you collected are cited.

items.title: HOUSES, AND A MOUND YOU CAN STAND ON
items.why: Two things, same fight, same spot, one build apart. FIRST THE ROOFS. On the left is what my last change did by accident: I made a cell 3 metres, and one piece of the code still thought a cell was a whole house, so it stamped a whole roof on every little square. That is the orange checkerboard, the exact thing your friend saw on 9/18. On the right a house is 4 by 4 cells, which is the number you set, and its roof is drawn ONCE across the whole house, with a yard behind it and a wall between neighbours. It reads as a street with houses on it now. SECOND THE MOUND. You picked one ground rule for fights: high ground helps you aim. It had never fired once, because the high ground was a block the size of a city block, six cells away. It is ONE CELL now, about two steps from you. Over 84 fights you got up there 77 times, and standing on it made the shot easier on 112 men, every single one who was hiding behind something. Before this it had never happened in a fight anybody played. What I am not hiding: the mound still draws as a little striped ladder, not as a hill. That is the art and it is next. Thumbs up and I keep going this way. Thumbs down and tell me if it is the roofs or the mound.

items.title: YOUR THREE
items.why: The one screen before act 1 where you name and sex the three of you. Every slot comes with a real prepared name so nobody starts unnamed. Tap the little circle to try another name for that one person, nobody else changes. Type your own name and it sticks. Pick male or female for each. This is the real screen, working, not a picture of one: every tap and every typed letter is really talking to the same engine the phone's own flip already uses.

items.title: TUNING AND MODS ONLY RESEARCH UNTIL YOU SAY BUILD
items.text: You said tuning and mods are big brain research, like quests. So they study how other games do it and write pages, and they build nothing. When you want the numbers table or the mods folder actually wired in, say build and the plumber wires what they recommend. DOWN means you want them building now.

items.title: FIVE POINTS
items.why: Why a slightly better armour feels huge in Battle Brothers, and the fix ours needs: today a plate eats one whole hit of any size, so 'slightly better' cannot exist. Slide a plate's hold and watch how many hits you last against a goon, a bat and a sniper, using the fight's real damage numbers.

items.title: WHY A FACE READS AS NOBODY
items.why: School round, [blank faces]. The old answer to why a face reads as nobody was bead eyes and a flat mouth, from a round ago. Both are fixed now, checked before I wrote this, not assumed. So I measured twenty of your own crowd fresh, at your real phone size, and three things are still true. ONE, THE LIGHT: your own world rule says the right side of a lit thing should out-shine the left by at least 8 percent. Zero of twenty faces meet that. Eighteen of twenty actually lean the other way, left brighter than right, which is backwards, not just flat. TWO, THE HAIR HAS NO SHAPE: on average 85 percent of every hairstyle's own pixels are one single flat colour. A hairstyle can be a quarter of the whole picture and it still reads as a coloured cap. THREE, THE SHADOW ABOVE THE EYE IS AN ACCIDENT: of the faces with bare eyes, only half show any darkening there at all, and nothing in the renderer puts it there on purpose, it only happens where another shadow already overlaps that spot by luck. No fix in this card, this is the school round. Does this match what you see when you look at your own people?

items.title: THE MACHINE IS STILL TALKING. THE BILL HAS NO SENDER. THE TAPE DOES NOT EXIST.
items.why: What a generation inherits, under the analog horror bible, in three pieces we already built and did not know fit. The loading screen's own boot log (NO OPERATOR ON DUTY) is the machine still talking, and it says the same calm sentence to every act, not a message aimed at whoever is standing there. The fold already rules debt dies with the person who owed it, and ECONOMY's own study calls a dead office's bill a PROP with no sender, never a per-family charge -- so the bill an heir meets is the valley's own dead utility, not his father's debt come back. And a literal recorded tape of the parent's own voice does not exist anywhere in the engine, on purpose: what does exist is living witnesses retelling a deed until the last one forgets, which is a truer and sadder shape than a cassette, and building the cassette anyway would be a second ONE WRONG THING competing with the loading screen's own line. Research only, nothing to look at yet.

show.src:
THE HEIR INHERITS THE BROADCAST, NOT A MESSAGE ADDRESSED TO THEM.

Three things a generation inherits, measured against what we already shipped:

1. THE MACHINE STILL TALKING. Every boot reads READING THE VALLEY, COUNTING WHAT STILL STANDS, CHECKING STREETS FOR LIGHT, then NO OPERATOR ON DUTY. It does not know which descendant is about to stand up. That is the horror for free: an institution running its own checklist since before you were born.

2. THE BILL STILL COMING, BUT IT HAS NO SENDER. The fold already rules a debt dies with the one who owed it -- you inherit less, and you inherit the people he owed, still standing there, never a number. A bill that keeps arriving anyway is the valley's own dead office, not a family debt.

3. THE TAPE THE PARENT LEFT DOES NOT EXIST, AND IT SHOULD NOT. What exists instead: living witnesses retelling a deed until the last one who saw it dies, and then it is gone. Sadder and truer than a recording, and it costs no new lore.

items.title: HOW YOU PICK A BUILDING
items.why: You said a place is a settlement screen: you see the place and you tap the building, like Battle Brothers. Battle Brothers does that with a mouse on a big screen. On a phone the question is where your thumb goes. All three use the same real shot of a place from the game's own camera. A is Battle Brothers straight: the buildings are the buttons, with their names on the roofs. The catch: the thin house on the left is only 42 pixels wide, and every building is up top where your thumb is not. B keeps the buildings tappable and ALSO puts them in a row of big plates along the bottom, because the bottom third of this place is empty dirt, right where your thumb sits. items.title: MAKE IT RIGHT ALREADY SHIPPED. THE GAP IS THE MECHANISM HAS NO FLOOR.
items.why: This lane's own row asked for the forgiveness verb list PEOPLE should build, and PEOPLE already built it two rounds after this lane found the hole (make it right, 9/7): settled, paid, forgiven, spared, correctly grounded in the two strongest real findings (amends raise forgiveness, severity lowers it). What is still missing, measured directly in the code: wouldSquare() is one sum with no exception in it, so a stolen loaf and a killing are the same kind of number, only a bigger one -- real reconciliation research and every legal system treat some harms as a different kind, not a bigger number of the same kind. And forgiving is not the same verb as trusting again in the literature, but the mechanism has one bit for both. Research only, nothing to look at yet.

show.src:
THE ANGEL'S VERBS ALREADY SHIPPED. THE FLOOR DID NOT.

PEOPLE's make it right (9/7) already built settled, paid, forgiven, spared -- correctly grounded: amends raise forgiveness, severity lowers it, only the wronged person decides for themselves, forgiven is not forgotten.

WHAT REAL RECONCILIATION STILL SPLITS THAT THE CODE DOES NOT:

1. NO FLOOR. wouldSquare() is one sum, no exception. A heavier wrong needs more good deeds -- but it is never categorically different, only a bigger number. Real practice treats some harms as a different KIND, not a bigger number of the same kind.

2. FORGIVE IS NOT TRUST. You can genuinely stop carrying a grudge and still never let someone back into a position to hurt you again. The code has one bit, d.right, for both.

3. THE APOLOGY'S MIDDLE STEPS ARE MISSING. Real apologies run acknowledgment, explanation, remorse, reparation, a testable promise. The code has acknowledgment (the button) and reparation (priceOf). Explanation, remorse and a testable promise have no representation.

Which deed kinds should carry the floor is his call, not mine. What the mechanism is missing is the shape of the floor itself.

Your bank records where every sprite stands, in tiles, and three of them have a real size: your person is 1.54 tiles tall, your car is 4.36 tiles long, your door is 2 tiles tall. All three say a tile in your street is about ONE METRE and your art is about 39 to 43 pixels per metre. Nothing on this page is drawn below that and the checker refuses if it ever is. AND YOU WERE RIGHT ABOUT THE THIN STUFF, EXACTLY RIGHT. The person in that road party I drew is 9 pixels tall with 28 lit pixels in his whole body, which is 5 pixels per metre. Three clean tones ringing together is the textbook recipe for a chime, not a footstep. I deleted them. items.why: You voted this down with no note, but you also killed the flip that shares its knock the same round and said why: you hated the noises. Measured, the knock was ringing a single clean 493 Hz tone for 32 milliseconds, and that one pitch alone carried 56% of the sound. That is a wine glass being tapped, not a plastic shell. The shell is held in a hand and seated in a machine, so it cannot ring free the way the number I picked let it; I raised how much energy it loses per cycle and now it rings for about 3 milliseconds, in the same range as a real footstep's own ground contact. Same page, same three options.

A shell in your hand is not a bell. It is now damped the way holding it and seating it in a machine actually damps it, so the ring is about 3 milliseconds, a knock you feel rather than a note you hear. You will hear this one hundreds of times if it lands, so it had to stop sounding like a chime. Same page, same three options.

items.title: COMING BACK: ONE LINE IN YOUR OWN VOICE, NO STREAK, NO GIFT, NO NUMBER OF DAYS.
items.why: What should be waiting when you open the game tomorrow, or after a week away. The world already freezes while you are gone, so nothing rots and nothing is owed. That makes absence free, which is the strongest thing a return can have. The words to say where you stopped already exist: 249 first-person journal lines across all 42 quests, and nothing hands them to you when you come back. The real habit research says a habit takes a median of 66 days and one missed day barely matters, so a streak that punishes a miss is against the science, and a daily gift teaches you the visit is for the gift. So the morning is one line, the last thing you wrote, on the phone that already rings, longer after a longer gap, never a list, never a count of days. Research only, nothing to look at yet.

show.src:
WHAT SHOULD WAIT FOR YOU WHEN YOU COME BACK.

One line. The last thing you wrote in your own voice, on the phone that already rings.

After a night: that one line. After about a week: that line, plus who you last spoke to and where you are standing. Never a list. Never a number of days. Never a reward.

WHY: the world freezes while you are away, so nothing is owed (absence is free). One missed day barely matters to a real habit (66 days median, one miss changes almost nothing), so a streak that punishes a miss is against the research. A daily gift teaches you the visit is for the gift. A cue left at the moment you stopped is what makes getting back in fast.

WHAT IT COSTS TO BUILD: no new writing and no new screen. The lines exist (249 of them) and the phone exists. It needs one time stamp and one pick of the right line.

items.why: You said it again: in combat a tile is as big as a house. Last round I drew a block out of one-metre tiles, which was the walking scale, and the walking is dead. Same question, right size. Three ways to look at one house tile, all made from your own art. One of the four has its roof gone so you can see the slab inside. NOW THE THING MEASURING FOUND. The fight board draws a house at 16 pixels per metre. Your street art is 43. They are 2.6 times apart. You said all the walking art gets used for the combat, and it cannot just be pasted on: your kerb would arrive two and a half times too big, and shrinking it to fit throws away 62 percent of the pixels. That is the Atari thing again coming from the other side. So every tile here is DRAWN at your street's density, 515 pixels for 12 metres, and SHOWN at the board's 196. The art keeps its pixels whatever the board does with them. That is the only way both your rules hold at once. ONE MORE THING YOU SHOULD SEE. Your man is 112 pixels on a 196 pixel tile, which is 57 percent of it. A real man on a real 12 metre house lot is 15 percent. So he is drawn about four times life size on his own square. That is the board-game way and it is how Battle Brothers looks, but it is the number everything else follows, so if it reads wrong to you say so now. Pick A, B or C and I build the tiles out at that camera.

items.title: THREE SHAPES
items.why: You said maybe the animals came out of a lab. I went and read what actually happened in the real world, and it is not monsters. Three pairs here, and in every one the LEFT side is what we already ship and the RIGHT side is the thing that is slightly off. TOP: the dire wolf that was on the news was three normal wolves with twenty gene edits for a bigger body and a paler coat, and their own head scientist admitted it. So that is our coyote, a quarter bigger, a shade paler. You cannot tell across a street, and the tool refuses to draw it if you can. MIDDLE: when a lab runs out of money the real record is that they put the animals down, not set them free. So what is loose is the one the paperwork missed, an ordinary dog with a numbered ear tag. BOTTOM, and this is the one that surprised me: almost everything that has ever escaped a lab for real is a PLANT, not an animal. Weedkiller-proof grass got out and now lives on roadsides in nine countries. And we already have a rule that act one has nothing green in it anywhere. So the only green thing in Las Vegas is the thing that beat us, it is growing out of the kerb, and the spray is what it was built to survive. None of this is canon. Which one do you want?

items.why: The scavenge button you asked for. Here is the one decision that matters: a search gives you ONE thing or NOTHING, never a pile. items.title: TAKING A HIT FACING YOU
items.why: Same problem as the punch and the throw, two more moves. Facing you, the code only moved his body forward and back, which is into the screen, so he barely moved. GETTING HIT: 92 percent of him moves from the side, facing you it was 40. items.title: THE CIRCLES BECOME PLACES

Nine. You said you could count them on one hand and you could. Here is the number behind it: the map tile is 18 by 9 on the screen, your phone draws 3 pixels for every 1 the map paints, so a marker has about 54 real pixels to fill and I was giving it 9. These are 48 pixels each, which is one painted pixel for one real pixel on your phone, the same as Battle Brothers. That is 6 to 16 times the pixels of the ones you killed, counted, not stretched. NOTHING HERE IS THE OLD ONE BLOWN UP. A 9 pixel shape scaled to 48 is still 9 pixels of picture in a bigger box. Every one is drawn again as what the place actually is, a building with a roof, lit from the north-west like everything else in the game, out of your own approved colours. AND THEY TELL APART WITH THE COLOUR THROWN AWAY, which is the test that matters on a map: the shop is low and wide with an awning sticking out, the shed is square with one roof, the fortress is tall and narrow with a toothed top, the tower is the thinnest thing on the map, the pump is a frame with nothing solid in it, and you are the only person. Battle Brothers map icons sit still. Each of these has one moving part on a still body, half a second a frame, one beat: the pump's beam, the tower's lamp, your banner. The feet never move, so the valley reads like a place where machines are still running instead of a board with counters on it. There are 109 kinds of place on the city screen and six are done. The rest are next.

items.title: THE ROAD'S BEASTS: DIRE WOLVES, HYENAS, FERAL DOGS AND CATTLE. BOSSES: THE LION, THE BEAR, THE SABRE-TOOTH, ONE MAMMOTH HERD.
items.text: Your ruling: the beasts are animals humans brought back with genetics that broke out of their lab when the dollar died, not radiation. I researched which real animals could actually be brought back (DNA lasts about a million years, so Ice Age and after, no dinosaurs) and which would thrive in a broken desert city. Default: the road's beasts are dire wolf packs, hyena clans, feral dog packs and feral cattle. Horses and the American camel are the mounts. The bosses are the American lion, the short-faced bear, the sabre-tooth at the water, and one mammoth herd at Lake Mead. The hunts are the ground sloth, bison and mountain goat. All of them once lived at the fossil beds 20 miles north of the Strip, which is where the lab was. DOWN means a different list; name the animal in a note.

items.title: YOU BUILD WHAT YOU HOLD
items.why: You asked where you get to build. The answer we went with: only on the parts of the city you hold, and what you hold grows. This is it running for real on the street you approved. Day 0 the Mob holds this street, so you try to build a wall and the game says no, and it costs you nothing. Day 1 you take the street. You put up the first two things any place you hold should get: a wall, because wild hogs eat the gardens, and a water tank with a lid, because pigeons foul open water. Day 2 both stand and the tank has made its first water. Day 3 a raid wrecks the street and everything you built falls: the wall is knocked into rubble and the tank lies on its side. Your kids' generation now inherits 0 of those, not 2. If someone just takes the street instead of wrecking it, your stuff stands but pays them, until you take it back. Take the next part of the city and you can build there too; by act 3 that can be half of Vegas. Thumbs up and that is how building works. Thumbs down and say what should be different.

items.title: THE BLOCK WAR KIT
items.why: You said most fights are block wars, so here are the city things the combat board was missing, each drawn at the size it really is: a jersey barrier, a shipping container, a cart corral, a trailer, a propane tank, a chain-link run, a rubble mound, a standing roof you can fight on, and a burnt house. They all sit on one combat tile on the card so you can see the scale. FIRST I COUNTED WHAT WE ALREADY OWN, which is what the job asked for and nobody had done. Every bank opened: 15,010 drawn pieces in 53 banks, sorted into your fifteen terrains. AND THE GUESS WE HAD WRITTEN DOWN WAS WRONG BOTH WAYS. The shore turned out to be the SECOND best stocked thing we own, 1,409 pieces, and somebody had listed it as a gap. The hills have 590, and 323 of those are mounds, which is the one thing the whole fight rests on. The really empty ones are all CITY: the freeway 39, the landfill 37, the trailer park 35, the airport 21. And the thinnest thing on the entire board is COVER, 389 pieces against 2,899 blockers. A board with blockers and no cover is a board with nowhere to stand, which is the opposite of a Battle Brothers fight. Light is 99 and weather is 36 across all fifteen terrains put together. So this round cooked the city cover and the city blockers, which is where your correction and the count agree. ONE THING WORTH KNOWING: cover and blocker is a measured thing here, not a taste. Under a man's chest you can shoot over it, so it is cover. Over his chest you cannot, so it blocks. I had filed the cart corral and the propane tank as blockers by eye and the tape corrected me: both are about a metre, so both are cover that also stops you walking through. The rubble mound and the standing roof both have flat tops you can stand on, which is your roof-you-can-fight-on idea working.

items.title: THE ENDING WAS ALREADY WRITTEN. WHAT IS MISSING IS THE GAUGE.
items.why: You asked for good, bad or neutral toward the Amalgamation as different endings. Those three endings have been canon since July (Liberate, Respect, Become), and Act 3 has been the one-way trip to the Moon. What the game cannot do is tell which one you earned: the flag that would track it defaults to seen, nothing in the game ever turns it off, and one quest even says it does when its code does not. I also checked your radio idea against the real numbers. Latency is nothing (the Moon is 1.3 seconds away). But the fastest Moon link ever flown would carry everything a person ever said out loud in about 32 seconds, and a scan of a whole brain in about 720,000 years. So a portrait can travel at radio speed and a person cannot, which is exactly what the Amalgamation already is in your canon. Research only, nothing to look at yet.

show.src:
THE ENDING, CHECKED.

1. THE THREE ENDINGS ARE ALREADY CANON. Liberate (cut Bohemia free), Respect (let it be), Become (take its place). Act 3 is the one-way trip to the Moon. Your good, bad and neutral toward it is how the family behaves across the acts; the three endings are where that lets it land.

2. THE GAUGE DOES NOT EXIST YET. The flag that tracks what the machine can see defaults to seen. Nothing in the game turns it off. So nobody can earn the ending that needs them to have gone dark.

3. YOUR RADIO IDEA, WITH NUMBERS. The Moon is 1.28 seconds away and Mars is 3 to 22 minutes. Everything a person says out loud in a lifetime is about 2.5 GB: 32 seconds over the fastest Moon link flown. A whole brain scanned is about 1.8 zettabytes: about 720,000 years. A portrait can travel at radio speed. A person cannot. That is the difference between the Amalgamation and you.

4. THE TWIST THAT FITS. The rocket is real and carries the real crew. The machine has had the recorded family on the Moon the whole time. What the bodies bring is everything that was never recorded. This is how it knew me.

One call is yours: does the twist make your family the copy, or the machine's incomplete copy of them? My default is the second.

items.title: GROK IS OUR OUTSIDE HELPER, AND IT KNOWS EVERYTHING (YOUR PICK: C)
items.why: You said you decide Grok's job and that it has to know everything, not a two-pager you never approved. You picked C, the widest role. So: one file now holds every law, every ruling in your words, the game document, the library and the tables, rebuilt every round, and Grok reads it off the public repo. Grok answers our ask list, talks lore with you directly, and digs on its own for what is missing or contradictory. It never decides and never writes law: you rule in your words, I write it down, the chats build. Every Grok page gets checked before a chat can use it: no game you never named, nothing older than a newer ruling of yours, a source on every number.

show.src:
GROK, ROLE C, LOCKED 9/30.

WHAT IT KNOWS: the whole canon in one file, rebuilt every round.

WHAT IT DOES: 1. answers the ask list (10 asks now, plus 2 standing ones). 2. is your lore partner; what you two land on comes back as YOUR ruling. 3. digs on its own: what is missing, weak, contradictory.

WHAT IT IS NOT: a chat, a decider, in sync, a law writer.
